name: Entra ID: revoke sign-in sessions (and optionally disable)
description: Run on a case: revokes all refresh tokens and session cookies of the case's user in Entra ID; if the case is tagged `entra-disable`, also blocks sign-in (accountEnabled = false). Writes a note with each HTTP status.

params.label: Entra tenant ID
params.help: Directory (tenant) ID from Entra admin center > Overview.

secrets.name: ENTRA_RESPONSE_CLIENT_ID
secrets.description: Application (client) ID of the Entra app registration used for containment.

secrets.name: ENTRA_RESPONSE_CLIENT_SECRET
secrets.description: Client secret value of that app registration used for containment.

setup:
### Entra side
1. Entra admin center > App registrations > **New registration** (single tenant, no redirect URI).
2. API permissions > Add a permission > Microsoft Graph > **Application permissions**: `User.RevokeSessions.All`, `User.EnableDisableAccount.All`, `User.Read.All`.
3. Click **Grant admin consent for <tenant>** (application permissions do nothing until an admin consents).
4. Certificates & secrets > **New client secret**; copy the secret *value* (not its ID). Note its expiry date.
5. Use a separate app registration from the read-only pull app. `User.EnableDisableAccount.All` + `User.Read.All` is the least-privileged pair for changing `accountEnabled`; drop both if you never disable accounts.
6. To disable users who hold Entra admin roles, Microsoft also requires the app to hold a sufficiently privileged admin role (see *Who can perform sensitive actions*); without it Graph answers 403 for those users.

### Here
1. Settings > Secrets: add the client ID and client secret below. Each must allow **both** `login.microsoftonline.com` (token request) and `graph.microsoft.com` (API call): the OAuth token is bound to the same hosts as the secrets that obtained it.
2. Install with `AZURE_TENANT_ID` = the Directory (tenant) ID.

Token: `POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/token` with `grant_type=client_credentials`, `scope=https://graph.microsoft.com/.default` ([client credentials flow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-client-creds-grant-flow)). The token is cached per worker until shortly before it expires and never stored.

### What it does
Target = the case's `username` attribute, else its first `email` artifact, used as the user principal name. With no target it only writes a note.
1. `POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/<upn>/revokeSignInSessions` (2xx = done; revocation can take a few minutes; external/guest users are not affected because they sign in through their home tenant).
2. Only if the case has the tag `entra-disable`: `PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/<upn>` with `{"accountEnabled": false}` (204 = done). Re-enable by patching `true`.
3. Note with both HTTP statuses.

Docs: [revokeSignInSessions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/user-revokesigninsessions?view=graph-rest-1.0), [Update user](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/user-update?view=graph-rest-1.0), [Who can perform sensitive actions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/users?view=graph-rest-1.0#who-can-perform-sensitive-actions).

## Containment guardrails
A **containment guard** step runs before the action: targets protected in **Settings → Integrations → Containment guardrails** (VIPs, domain controllers, critical ranges) are never contained automatically, and the tenant's daily and per-case caps apply. A refusal stops the run and adds a case note; every action is listed on the case under **Artifacts & assets → Containment**, where an analyst marks it released once undone.
